message:
fix(notification): a transient delivery failure marks no destination refused

Envelope reads every report from the return path as a refusal
(ADR-0078), so an occasion that ran out of retries used to stamp an
address FAILED on the strength of an outage. The reporting loop now
skips anything that is not a permanent failure; a mixed occasion still
reports the refused mobile and only it.

feat(notification): a correction, a void and a completion cancel pointless invitations

Three reactors dispatch CancelPendingInvitations, scoped to the
addressed recipient on a correction so another recipient's pending
invitation is left alone. A redelivered correction no longer cancels its
own re-invitation: requested_at is stored at whole seconds while the
correction's instant keeps microseconds.

docs(task-055): every surface that described one retry ladder now says what is true

A delivery is retried on its profile's schedule, one whose retries run
out ends FAILED with a transient kind, and only a provider's permanent
refusal is reported to Envelope. Also fixes a test string whose
apostrophe was a parse error.

docs(task-055): name both return paths, record the retry schedules, accept ADR-0079

The reference prose now says Notification reads an (envelope, recipient)
pair on the success path as well as the failure one, and the
architecture overview describes per-kind retry and the transient FAILED
ending. The owner accepted ADR-0079 on 2026-10-09, with the broker delay
still to be observed.

test(task-055): kill the surviving mutants on the delivery-reliability lines

Infection left 41 survivors on changed lines; the new tests kill 32 of
them, each checked by reverting the line it covers.
Merge develop into feat/delivery-reliability: TASK-031, 057, 058 and 059 records

Merge feat/delivery-reliability: a delivery is retried, ends, and is rechecked

TASK-055 (ADR-0079). Notices retry at 60, 300 and 900 s and codes at 5,
15 and 30 s, never past the code's send window; a delivery whose retries
run out ends FAILED instead of staying PENDING; a stale late invitation
ends NOT_NEEDED; a transient failure never reaches Envelope. Full suite,
lint, deptrac and PHPStan pass.

feat(envelope): a recipient's invitation state is derived from its recorded instants

The Envelope contract gains the invitation vocabulary (purpose, outcome,
unsent kind, state) and the single function that derives a state from
the recorded instants. Both new delivery events carry the channel beside
the destination kind, which tells a WhatsApp refusal from an SMS that
landed.

feat(envelope): a recipient records an invitation left unsent, and why

envelope.recipient gains invitation_unsent_at and
invitation_unsent_kind, kept together by a CHECK, and the write port
records each invitation outcome once without ever stamping a closed leg
failed. The delivery event docblocks now say where an address lives and
state the record-on-change rule.

fix(envelope): a delivery trace keeps its observation instant to the microsecond

The repository wrote observed_at as whole seconds, so a redelivered
report against the same observation recorded a second outcome. Tests now
push each invitation outcome and refusal through a real database and the
event log once, with a closed key set and no address.

feat(notification): an invitation owed to a recipient with no address is recorded unsent

Step activation, contact correction and resend used to skip such a
recipient in silence. The crossing test runs the use cases against the
real Envelope adapter: a refused channel beside a landed one moves only
its destination, and both refused record one verdict in either order.

feat(envelope): the sender reads each recipient's invitation state and instants

The recipient in GET /envelopes/{id} carries invitation_state, three
instants and the unsent kind. A release reason's dormant branch now asks
for the send instant alone, and the invitation prose states the link's
real lifetime and which release reasons nothing produces yet.

test(task-056): the audit trail folds and reads the two invitation facts

The test builder's registry learns RecipientInvitationOutcomeRecorded
and RecipientDestinationRefused. Prose that called a delivery success
silent, or NOT_REACHED the unreachable-recipient case, is corrected, and
ADR-0078 section 5 cites the tests that pin the read model.

fix(task-056): a transient failure marks no destination on the trace-only path

An outage says nothing about an address or a number, so
PropagateDestinationRefusalUseCase now acts only on a permanent failure.
The domain models and ADR-0078/0079 state the delivery facts as
realized, and the two Propagate use cases cite each other by qualified
name.

Merge feat/delivery-facts: invitation outcomes come back to Envelope as facts

TASK-056. A refused channel beside one that landed marks only its
destination on the trace; every invitation outcome is an Envelope event
with no address in it; a recipient owed an invitation and given none is
recorded as not sent; the sender reads each recipient's invitation
state.

feat(task-031): order an occasion's deliveries and let a tenant carry an SMS capability

notification_delivery gains a position, unique per occasion, so
deliveries come back in the order they were targeted. The channel on
Envelope's invitation events becomes the closed enum InvitationChannel,
and identity.tenant gets an SMS flag, off by default, set by a third
system command (ADR-0077).

feat(task-031): a tenant's SMS capability, switchable by an operator from the console

app:identity:sms-notifications <tenant> --enable|--disable dispatches
SetTenantSmsNotifications. ADR-0077 section 2.4 makes SMS available only
to a tenant that has been enabled for it, and other contexts read the
flag through Identity's contract.

feat(task-031): an IN_ORDER occasion sends its head and falls back on a failure

DeliveryPolicy gains IN_ORDER, which folds like ANY: the Notification
aggregate materializes every target and sends the first, falling back to
the next in the same unit of work. Tests now run the tenant flag through
the real repository and log, and every list of the provisioning role's
grants names its column grant on identity.tenant.

feat(task-031): Envelope resolves channels from tenant SMS capability and phone

SMS is available only when Identity says the tenant has the capability
and this deployment can send to the number's country. The phone port
names its third answer, countryOf(), and the SMS country refusal says
when it fires. recordSent's docblock explains why IN_ORDER siblings
still need no coordination.

feat(task-031): refuse a notification-channel declaration that cannot be met

NotificationChannelsGuard holds ADR-0077 section 2.5's authoring checks
in two halves, availability and contact, each cause with its own code.
OTP_SMS to a mobile outside the supported countries is refused by
country. The test builders now declare ["EMAIL"] unless a test says
otherwise.

test(task-031): declare recipients' channels in Signature Execution and Session fixtures

Each AddRecipient and each created recipient names ["EMAIL"] explicitly,
the value the default already gave, so making the field required later
leaves these tests unchanged. The two refusals' docblocks now say what
they cover and where the country comes from.

test(task-031): declare recipients' channels in the Envelope persistence and unit tests

Every recipient these fixtures create names its channels instead of
relying on the default, so making the field required changes nothing
here.

feat(task-031): the channel selector turns a recipient's declared channels into a policy

DefaultChannelSelector takes the channels a recipient's declaration
resolved to (DeclaredChannels) rather than assuming email. The closed-
leg, authoring and entity tests declare EMAIL explicitly, and the
claim's docblock names both deferred checks.

feat(task-031): the integrator declares a recipient's notification channels

POST /recipients accepts notification_channels and notification_mode
(still optional in this expand step) and warns when one factor is
declared twice. The selector's service comment is brought up to date and
the add-recipient acceptance bodies start sending the field.

feat(task-031): re-invitations and resends reach a recipient on their declared channels

Both reactions drop their email === null skip for the same resolution
the step-activation invitation uses. A landline declared for SMS is
refused whatever the mode, and the 422 texts say so.

feat(task-031): ending notices follow each recipient's list

The completed and ended reactions resolve each recipient's declared
channels instead of skipping a recipient without an email, and a
delegated recipient whose step activated is told the envelope ended.

feat(task-031): the sender changes a recipient's channels without spending a correction

Envelope::changeRecipientNotificationChannels() replaces a recipient's
declared channels while the envelope is still open and records the
change as a fact, with a flag saying whether it re-invites.

feat(task-031): the integrator changes a recipient's notification channels over HTTP

PUT /api/v1/envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/notification-
channels (machine key) takes notification_channels and mode. Its 422
text refuses a landline whatever the mode, as the other routes do, and
the ending-notice prose now names the delegated half of the audience.

feat(task-031): a re-inviting channel change cancels the old invitation and invites anew

When Envelope records RecipientNotificationChannelsChanged with
reinvites true, Notification reacts twice: it cancels the pending
invitations, then invites on the new list. The resend route now names
every refusal, and the signing-tokens route says a correction retires a
link.

feat(trail): a party's personal group has slots for the decline and browser report

ADR-0072 foresees browser-reported evidence as an empty slot of the
trail; the model now carries it, with Accept-Language beside it.
Session's act context also carries the documents its recipient may read
apart from those they sign, and the browser's report exists as values
that refuse an impossible shape.

feat(task-045): trust no proxy until one is declared, and never a forwarded host

framework.trusted_proxies reads SYMFONY_TRUSTED_PROXIES explicitly,
committed empty in .env. ReportedEvidence is one closed value that names
each dropped part by path and reason, never by value, and a coordinate,
accuracy or pixel ratio that is not a finite number is refused (NaN
passed every range check).

test(task-031): every notifying site answers what the one resolution answers

OneResolutionTest feeds one recipient through declaration, contacts,
trace, tenant capability and deployment wiring, and checks that each
notifying site agrees. Enabling SMS leaves an email recipient on email.

feat(task-031): a recipient is added only with a declared channel list

The contract step of ADR-0077's expand/contract: POST /recipients now
refuses an absent or null notification_channels with a 422, and neither
controller turns a null into [] any more, so an absent list can never
become "send nothing". A phone-only carrier is invited by SMS with a
working link.

feat(session): the closing act records the browser's report and Accept-Language

SigningSession keeps what the signer's browser reported and the Accept-
Language the platform observed, once the signing gate has passed; a
decline also records its observed address. An ill-formed part of a
report is dropped by its unit and recorded rather than refused.

feat(session): the session row keeps the browser report in its own reported_* columns

A migration adds seventeen nullable reported_* columns and
signer_accept_language, with a CHECK that refuses a row breaking the
shape. Reported times keep their microseconds, and POST /signing/commit
reads an optional evidence member and the Accept-Language header.

fix(task-031): an envelope's recipients come back in one order on every read

Both repositories ordered by step ordinal alone, so recipients sharing a
step came back in whatever order the database chose. ADR-0078 section
2.2 is amended for the closed InvitationChannel, and the records that
described email-only routing carry dated notes.

feat(session): a decline records its observed address, user agent and the browser's report

POST /signing/decline now mirrors the commit: an optional evidence
member and the Accept-Language header, kept once the signing gate has
passed. The published spec gains the BrowserEvidence component, since
the signer sends nothing until it is documented (BL-177).

refactor(session): name the evidence contract for the act that closed the session

A decline records the observed IP address and user agent on the session
row just as a commit does, so the commit-only evidence reader and view
are renamed for the act, a commit or a decline.

fix(session): the BrowserEvidence descriptions in the published spec are single paragraphs

The component's YAML had a blank line between every line, so the folded
description began with a newline and broke the generated text.

feat(session): another context reads the act's Accept-Language and the browser's report

ActEvidenceView gains acceptLanguage() and reported(), an Option of a
new reported-evidence view, for a decline as for a commit. The view's
census now classifies every field of a reading entry and of a drop.

feat(trail): the trail states each party's browser report and the decline's values

A party whose leg the recipient closed through the platform's ceremony
now shows what Session holds of its browser report, plus the decline's
IP, browser and Accept-Language, in the JSON and the PDF. A report with
nothing sent prints one line, and short reading times print in seconds.

fix(task-031): the channel-list CHECK refuses a non-array without raising

The list-shape function walked the value with jsonb_array_elements and
relied on the CHECK's AND to test the type first. The channel-change
route gets its missing 401 and cross-tenant cases, a warning's channel
becomes a published enum, and the models, schema reference and ADRs
describe channels the sender declares.

test(task-045): a commit and a decline carrying the browser's report answer as before

Three tests drive the real commit route through the relay and the
trail's assembly, and check that the rows and trails hold the report.
ADR-0072 fills its browser-reported slot, and five stale statements are
corrected to match the branch.

test(task-031): pin channel refusals, defaults and re-invitation after the mutation run

Each test fails on a mutant the changed-line Infection run left alive,
e.g. a provisioned tenant reporting SMS on. Three no-op steps the run
showed could not change behaviour are dropped, such as an early return
on an empty list in NotificationChannelsGuard.

test(task-045): pin the intake and the reported value objects where mutants escaped

Covers the intake's device, text, clock, reading-cap and coordinate
handling, and the hydration of the reported columns: each wrong-typed or
wrong-shaped value is refused, and a one-value device reads back as a
device.

Merge feat/channel-selection: a recipient declares the channels that reach them

TASK-031, under ADR-0077. Every recipient carries a required
notification_channels list, plus notification_mode when it names two
channels, and every notifying site resolves it through one function. An
empty list means the integrator delivers the link; a list that resolves
nothing is recorded as not sent. SMS needs both the tenant capability
and the deployment's support.
Merge develop into feat/browser-reported-evidence: with TASK-031's channel selection

Merge feat/browser-reported-evidence: TASK-045 - the browser's evidence reaches the trail

Both take an optional evidence block (geolocation with its denial,
device context, document reading), read leniently: an ill-formed part is
dropped and recorded by path and reason, never a reason to refuse the
act. A decline now records the IP, user agent and Accept-Language; the
values sit in reported_* columns and the audit trail states each with
the browser as its source.

feat(task-059): the audit trail publishes each party's invitations

The assembler builds one entry per invitation outcome or refused
destination from Envelope's two invitation facts (ADR-0078 section 2.5),
in log order with purpose, outcome, channel, instant and masked
destination. A claimable slot claimed before its step activated is due
its invitation, and is unstated without one.

feat(task-037): a claimed recipient is invited once, under the activation's cause token

A claim landing on a step that is already active fired nothing, because
the activation fan-out had skipped the unclaimed slot. The envelope read
now tells an unclaimed slot from a claimed recipient who has not acted
(recipients[] gains declared_claimable and claimed_at), and the record
is rewritten against today's Notification area.

test(task-059): a downloaded trail states how the invitation travelled

One signer is invited by email through the send route, the relay runs
the delivery, the signature and the seal, and the trail downloaded
afterwards states the invitation. A stream from before the invitation
facts renders and says it recorded none.

fix(evidence-audit): an invitation with no recorded outcome is stated as exactly that

A party whose step activated with no invitation fact was labelled
NOT_RECORDED_BY_PLATFORM, whose label suggested the platform never
tried. ADR-0072 gains the invitation destination rule, and the closed-
now fixture rows are written under the actors Notification's subscribers
use.

feat(notification): a claim on an already-active step invites the named party

OnRecipientClaimed turns RecipientClaimed into NotifyClaimedRecipient,
and the use case decides. ADR-0057 section 2.7 is recorded as built, and
the recipient's closed key set test now includes the claimable slot's
two facts.

docs(adr-0057): accepted, every clause exercised

The owner promoted ADR-0057 on 2026-10-14 once TASK-037 had built the
claim's invitation under the shared cause token. The notification and
envelope models state that a claim invites the named party.

test(trail): a step activated twice is judged by its first activation

Pins the break in the assembler's invitation loop that Infection left
escaped.

Merge feat/trail-invitations: the audit trail states how each party's invitation travelled

TASK-059. Each party's personal group gains invitations: one entry per
outcome or refused destination, in log order, with masked destination.
An activated party with no recorded outcome is stated as such, and a
sent invitation lists the DELIVERY_RECEIPT_NOT_RECORDED limitation. The
JSON change is additive and the schema stays f5sign.audit-trail/1.
Merge develop into feat/claimed-recipient-invitation: with TASK-059's trail invitations

fix(trail): a claimable slot claimed at any time is due its invitation

TASK-059 stated an empty invitations list for a slot claimed after its
step activated, since nothing recorded one. Without a fact it is now
unrecorded, and the render test and the acceptance criterion say so.

Merge feat/claimed-recipient-invitation: TASK-037 - a claimed recipient is invited once

A claim on a step that is already active now invites the named party
through NotifyClaimedRecipientUseCase. It shares the activation's cause
token, so the two paths converge in every order. GET /envelopes/{id}
gains declared_claimable and claimed_at so the sender can see a slot
that still waits for a name, and a handoff note tells the dashboard.

feat(actor): an operator acting from the console is a system actor inside a tenant

SystemActorId::operator() mints the operator: prefix for a person
operating the platform, and OtpSendLimitsCleared is the fact an unblock
leaves on the log (ADR-0077 section 2.10). ActorIdTest's unknown-kind
row moves to a prefix neither vocabulary has.

feat(session): OTP sends to one phone are bounded per envelope and, loosely, across them

The single destination counter becomes two per medium: a narrow one
keyed on destination and envelope, and a wide one across envelopes. The
limiter can now clear one person's counters, never the source-address
one, and the resend route's 409 names the SMS cap refusal.

feat(task-058): a notification delivery has a requested and a settled instant

notification_delivery gains nullable requested_at and settled_at,
backfilled only where the occasion's request time is true. MaskedContact
moves to Foundation so the trail and the notification history share one
mask without Notification importing Evidence & Audit.

feat(notification): a cross-tenant funnel counts each tenant's SMS deliveries

notification.sms_volume_since(p_since) is a SECURITY DEFINER function
owned by a new NOLOGIN role and returns nothing else.
Envelope::unblockResends() also lets an operator's grant raise a
recipient's SMS resend cap, and records it as RecipientResendsUnblocked.

feat(session): an operator can clear the OTP send counters holding one recipient

app:session:clear-otp-limits enters the named tenant and dispatches
ClearOtpSendLimits, and tells the operator the source-address counter
stays. The resend grant persists in envelope.recipient.resend_allowance
(NOT NULL, CHECK >= 0), and the volume funnel's prose says what it
counts.

feat(notification): every delivery transition stamps its instant from the Clock

The aggregate stamps requested_at when it asks the channel and
settled_at when the delivery ends. Both are persisted and read back
together, so they survive the next save of the delivery upsert.

feat(notification): a recipient's notification history is read masked, one page at a time

The history handler asks Envelope's contract for the envelope first, and
answers an unknown envelope, another tenant's and an unknown recipient
alike. The query carries the raw cursor and a malformed one is refused
before anything is read.

feat(notification): an hourly report names each tenant over the SMS threshold

app:notification:report-sms-volume counts the last hour's SMS per tenant
through the cross-tenant funnel. An operator's resend grant is applied
under the envelope's row lock so concurrent grants serialise, and the
resend-allowance migration states what its backfilled 0 means in each
aggregate state.

feat(notification): a tenant reads every message sent to one recipient, masked and paged

GET /api/v1/envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/notifications is
Notification's first HTTP route. DbalNotificationHistory reads a page of
occasions and their deliveries with one bounded statement, and the query
is built from the route's path ids as strings because the UI layer may
not name Envelope's types.

test(notification): pin the SMS volume report threshold; label operator facts on the trail

A tenant exactly at the threshold is now the unnamed case. Naming
another tenant's envelope on an operator console is refused and writes
nothing. The resend grant and the OTP clear get labels on the audit
trail, which the full run's census tests required.

docs(task-057): code prose, ADRs and backlog record the SMS spend guards as built

The destination key became two counters, so the send route refuses five
ways. ADR-0077 section 2.10 is written in the past tense, and the
operator's two trail facts carry short labels like their neighbours.

fix(notification): the history route's 400 names each code it answers

A present but malformed F5Sign-Declared-Subject header answers
INVALID_DECLARED_SUBJECT rather than BAD_REQUEST. Every criterion is now
cited by a test, the route's machine-key declaration is asserted, and
markSent's docblock states the failure transitions that exist.

fix(actor): an operator label is bounded and printable before it reaches the log

SystemActorId::operator() refused only a blank label, so a console could
write an unbounded one or one with control characters. The unblock and
clear-limits commands also carried the label twice; the fact now records
the one its issuer carries.

docs(notification): record the recipient history route and its two delivery instants

LIVE_SCHEMA and the Notification domain model gain requested_at and
settled_at. Paging tests refuse a trailing newline, leading whitespace
and an impossible base64 length, which the changed-line mutation run had
left unpinned.

docs(adr): ADR-0077 is accepted, every decision realized by TASK-031 and TASK-057

The owner accepted it on 2026-10-19 once TASK-057 had realized section
2.10. The schema and domain models state the SMS resend cap, the four
OTP counters and the volume funnel.

docs(adr-0078): delivery outcomes come back as facts is accepted

The owner accepted it on 2026-10-19 once TASK-058 realized section 2.7
with the notification history.

Merge feat/notification-history: TASK-058 - the sender reads a recipient's messages

GET /envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/notifications lists a
recipient's occasions with each delivery's channel, masked destination,
status, failure kind and requested and settled instants, keyset-paged,
with one 404 for anything the caller may not see. notification_delivery
gains the two instants, and ADR-0078 is accepted. The full suite passes.

Merge develop into feat/sms-spend-guards: with TASK-058's notification history

Three conflicts, each two independent additions in one place, kept both:
the backlog rows, and two others.

fix(notification): bind the SMS volume port by name now that its directory is excluded

The develop merge excluded Notification/Domain/ReadRepository from
autodiscovery, so SmsVolume needs an explicit binding. The volume
fixtures also pass the provider reference and instants that recordSent,
recordFailed and recordNotNeeded now require, and two surviving mutants
on the resend cap get tests.

test(session): pin the destination counters, unpriced phone media and the clear consoles

Surviving mutants showed four unpinned behaviours, among them clearing
the wide destination counter. Both operator consoles now have tests that
read what they print on each refusal and that padded options are
trimmed, including the largest accepted grant.

test(session): an OTP clear skips a delivered method whose destination is missing

A recipient declaring OTP_SMS with no phone has a known medium and no
destination; nothing pinned that the clear skips it.

Merge feat/sms-spend-guards: TASK-057 - SMS spend is bounded where a person can run it up

A recipient reached by SMS is refused a sixth invitation resend with
RECIPIENT_RESEND_CAP_REACHED (409), and an operator raises the cap with
app:envelope:unblock-resends. The OTP destination limiter spends a
narrow and a wide counter, and app:session:clear-otp-limits clears one
person's counters but never the source-address one. An operator acting
from the console is a system actor.

fix(storage): a locked put or copy sends its retain-until date in the form Linode accepts

async-aws writes x-amz-object-lock-retain-until-date as ATOM with a
+00:00 offset, which Linode refuses; it is now sent in UTC with a Z. A
copy also records the version it wrote when the backend does not name
one, as Linode does for a CopyObject into a versioned container.

Merge fix/linode-object-lock: conserved bytes reach the retained container on Linode

The custodian's promotion and trail conservation failed on every run in
production: Linode refused the lock date async-aws writes, and a copy
there names no version. The date is now sent in UTC with a Z, and a copy
whose answer omits its version reads it back.

feat(envelope): a resend may name a declared channel, refused if undeclared or unreachable

Envelope::resendInvitation() takes an optional channel, and
envelope.recipient.sms_resends_made counts only resends that may go out
by SMS, backfilled from resends_made where the declaration includes SMS.
ADR-0080 is recorded as Proposed, amending ADR-0077 sections 2.8 and
2.10.

feat(notification): a resend naming a channel goes on that channel alone or is unsent

ResendRecipientInvitation carries the named channel from the route to
the aggregate and on to the resend reaction (ADR-0080 section 2.4). The
SMS resend cap now counts a resend naming SMS, or naming nothing for a
recipient who declared it.

test(resend): a resend naming SMS goes out as one SMS over HTTP

Drives the real route, the relay and Notification with a recording SMS
transport, and checks that the refusals answer as specified. The route
comment, the corrected-recipient prose and the request docblock no
longer say the cap applies to every recipient who declares SMS.

docs(adr): ADR-0080 is accepted, and every surface that called it proposed says so

The owner accepted it on 2026-10-19; TASK-060 exercises every decision.
The channel refusals' text, the named-channel resolution and the resend
request are pinned by tests, and the cross-flow acceptance test declares
CoversNothing like the other flows.

Merge feat/resend-channel: TASK-060 - a resend may name a declared channel

An integrator can ask for one resend on EMAIL or SMS without changing
the recipient's declaration; the channel must be declared and reach
them. The SMS resend cap counts only resends that may go out by SMS,
kept in a per-recipient count. ADR-0080 is accepted and amends ADR-0077.

docs(adr): ADR-0061 states that an operator's name is kept in clear in the event log

Section 2.10 said the actor column carries no personal data, but since
TASK-057 the operator consoles record the operator's label there.

feat(notification): every email ends its footer with the full envelope reference

The invitation, completion, ending and delivered one-time-code occasions
now save envelope_ref among their variables. The email is the one place
a recipient still holds a reference when the signing link fails, so the
shared footer prints it.

test(envelope-reference): a delivery pinned before the reference still transmits

Archives the pre-reference copy of the invitation, saves a notification
pinned to it with the old variables, and checks that it still goes out.
The single-recipient scenario cites its criteria, and the notification
model states that every email's footer prints the envelope id.

feat(otp-limits): each gate of one session spends its own session counter

The access gate's sends and the signing gate's sends shared one counter,
because the session key was a digest of the session alone. ADR-0081
gives each gate its own budget and is recorded as Proposed; the operator
rescue clears both.

feat(otp-limits): SMS limits are 5 per gate, 10 per phone on an envelope, 30 per address

The access gate's retries alone spent the old three-an-hour SMS session
budget when one code was slow; the numbers now match email's. A test
pins the number of every otp_* policy the yaml declares, so an added
policy cannot land without one.

Merge feat/envelope-reference-in-emails: TASK-061 - every email footer has the envelope id

The signer quotes it to support when the link fails; it is the id the
signing read-model returns as envelope.id. Email only, plain text, never
a link; SMS is unchanged. The full suite passes.

docs(otp-limits): the limiter and the send route name the session counter per gate

Both class docblocks and the Signing Session status row listed four
counters as per session; since ADR-0081 the session counter is per
session and gate. The refusal parity test also pins that the split adds
nothing to the wire.

docs(adr): ADR-0081 is accepted, exercised by TASK-062

The owner accepted it on 2026-10-20 once the branch exercised every
decision in its section 2.
Merge develop into feat/otp-budget-per-gate: brings TASK-061's email footer reference

Merge feat/otp-budget-per-gate: TASK-062 - each signing gate has its own send budget

A recipient who needed three SMS codes to get in could not be sent the
code to sign. The session counter is now keyed on session and gate
(ADR-0081): signing and declining share the signing gate's budget, and
destination and source counters stay shared. SMS limits rise to 5 per
gate, 10 per phone on one envelope and 30 per source address; the 429 is
unchanged.

feat(task-064): a change to a recipient's gates is a published Envelope fact

RecipientAuthRequirementChanged carries both declarations verbatim and
two structural flags. ADR-0083 is accepted: a recipient's gates are
editable until they first open their link. An opening is refused when
the access gate changed since it was read.
